newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Bank of Korea sees 1997 GDP growth at 5.5-6.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Korea sees 1997 GDP growth at 5.5-6.0 pct.

text.p: The Bank of Korea said on Friday it was revising its forecast for South Korea's gross domestic product (GDP) growth this year to a real 5.5-6.0 percent from 6.4 percent.
The central bank said the country's current account deficit could exceed its earlier forecast of $18 billion in 1997, which compared with a $23.72 billion shortfall last year.
The consumer price index, a major indicator for inflation, is expected to grow by 4.7 percent this year against a 4.5 percent rise in 1996, it said in a statement.
It projected a GDP growth of five percent each for the first and second quarter of this year, against rises of 7.8 percent and 6.9 percent, respectively, a year earlier.
The growth in the second half of this year was put at around six percent. GDP grew 6.9 percent in the same 1996 period.

Current account deficit for the first and second quarters were forecast at $7.8 billion and $4.8 billion respectively. Last year, the shortfall was $4.64 billion in the first quarter and $5.24 billion in the second quarter.

The bank said it expected a rise in prices of the nation's major export items, including computer memory chips, steel and petrochemical products, which would help reduce the current account deficit in the second quarter.
